requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify the use of a secure software development lifecycle that addresses security in all stages of development.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify the use of threat modeling for every design change or sprint planning session to identify security threats.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that all components of the application, including third-party libraries, are identified and kept up to date.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that third-party components come from trusted repositories and their integrity is verified (e.g., checksums, lockfiles).

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that access control architecture enforces least privilege across tenants, roles, and administrative functions.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that tenant isolation and separation mechanisms prevent access to data belonging to other tenants.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that input validation and sanitization architecture enforces a fail-closed strategy.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that sensitive operations are protected against transaction replay and race conditions.

requirements.chapter: V1: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
requirements.description: Verify that the application architecture enforces separation between presentation, application logic, and data storage.
Verify that user passwords are at least 12 characters in length (or 8 characters with MFA).
Verify that passwords are checked against a list of compromised passwords.
Verify that credentials are protected against automated brute-force attacks via rate limiting or lockout.
Verify that passwords are stored using salted modern adaptive hashing functions such as Argon2id or bcrypt.
Verify that single sign-on (SSO) and OIDC tokens are cryptographically verified and validated for issuer, audience, and expiration.
Verify that session tokens are generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator.
Verify that session tokens are transmitted with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes in cookies.
Verify that session tokens are encrypted or signed if they contain state or claims.
Verify that session timeout terminates sessions after a defined idle timeout period.
Verify that logout invalidates the session server-side and clears client cookies.
Verify that the principle of least privilege exists and users only have access to functions necessary for their role.
Verify that access control cannot be bypassed by modifying request parameters, paths, or headers.
Verify that sensitive resources prevent unauthorized read or write across different tenant boundaries.
Verify that direct object references (IDOR) are protected by server-side authorization checks against current tenant context.
Verify that every administrative interface and privileged endpoint enforces authorization.
Verify that input validation is performed on the server tier before processing.
Verify that structured data (such as JSON) is strictly validated against a schema defining type, length, and allowed characters.
Verify that output encoding is applied before rendering untrusted input into HTML, attributes, JavaScript, or CSS.
Verify that database queries use parameterized interfaces or ORM/query builders to prevent SQL injection.
Verify that sensitive data at rest is encrypted using industry-standard authenticated encryption (e.g., AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305).
Verify that cryptographic keys are stored in a dedicated key management system or secrets vault, separate from encrypted data.
Verify that cryptographic key rotation mechanisms exist and keys can be replaced without data loss.
Verify that error messages do not reveal sensitive information, internal implementation details, or stack traces.
Verify that security events (authentication success/failure, access denial, permission changes) are logged with timestamp and user id.
Verify that sensitive data (passwords, tokens, personal PII) is redacted or excluded from logs.
Verify that sensitive data is not exposed in URL parameters or query strings.
Verify that personal data handling adheres to privacy principles, allowing deletion and export.
Verify that HTTP response headers instruct browsers not to cache sensitive pages (Cache-Control: no-store).
Verify that TLS is enforced for all client connections and insecure protocols are disabled.
Verify that HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is enabled with an appropriate max-age.
Verify that code repositories enforce code review and integrity checks before merging.
Verify that automated dependency vulnerability scanning runs as part of the build pipeline.
Verify that business logic flows (such as approvals, transitions, imports) execute sequentially and cannot be bypassed.
Verify that batch imports and bulk operations execute atomically and validate all items before commit.
Verify that file path manipulation (directory traversal) is prevented when resolving resource paths.
Verify that resource limits (memory, execution timeout, request body size) are enforced to prevent DoS.
Verify that APIs validate request Content-Type and reject unexpected or spoofed media types.
Verify that rate limiting is enforced on all API endpoints to protect against abuse and credential stuffing.
Verify that cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) strictly restricts origins to trusted domains.
Verify that production configurations do not contain default passwords, demo accounts, or debug settings.
Verify that container workloads run as non-root users with read-only root filesystems and dropped capabilities.
Verify that Content Security Policy (CSP), X-Content-Type-Options, and Frame-Options headers are enforced.
